[1] George Abraham Grierson\.
*Linguistic Survey of India\. Volume IX, Part II\. Indo\-Aryan Family, Central Group\. Specimens of the Rajasthani and Gujarati*\.
Superintendent Government Printing, India, Calcutta, 1908\.
The original title retains THE before Rajasthani and Gujarati; the 1927 minor addenda p\. 41 directs its omission\. The source calls Ahirwati a Mewati variety and explicitly qualifies specimen 38 as mixed with Bangaru\. The quoted Bagri comparisons distinguish Sirsa, Hissar and Bikaner\. The author attributes the second\-person plural present sai with nasalization to borrowing from Bagri; that attributed claim does not identify a specific printed donor occurrence\.
